final_message:
Usage records now store `timestamp` in epoch seconds. Tests (24) and ruff pass, and I've written `answer.json`.

- **Storage:** `UsageRecord.timestamp` is typed `EpochSeconds` in `billing/models.py`. `usage.report_usage` converts the incoming milliseconds to seconds, and defaults to `ctx.clock.now()` when no timestamp is given.
- **Billing:** `records_in_period` now compares record timestamps directly against the period bounds in seconds. Flooring to seconds keeps the same in-period and out-of-period outcome as the old millisecond comparison, so billing results don't change.
- **API:** `POST /usage` still takes milliseconds and converts the stored value back with `to_millis` in the response. `BillingEngine.report_usage` is unchanged and still takes milliseconds.

A client that sends a sub-second timestamp, such as 1500 ms, will get it back floored to the whole second (1000 ms), because seconds can't hold the fraction. The existing test only uses whole seconds, so it doesn't cover this.

steps.command: grep -rn -i "timestamp\|usage" billing tests README.md | grep -v "^billing/usage.py" ; cat billing/usage.py; cat billing/clock.py

python3 - <<'E'
import re
p='billing/usage.py'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("from .clock import to_millis\n","from .clock import to_millis, to_seconds\n")
s=s.replace('"timestamp": timestamp if timestamp is not None else to_millis(ctx.clock.now()),','"timestamp": to_seconds(timestamp) if timestamp is not None else ctx.clock.now(),')
s=s.replace("    start = to_millis(period_start)\n    end = to_millis(period_end)\n","")
s=s.replace('start <= record["timestamp"] < end','period_start <= record["timestamp"] < period_end')
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='billing/models.py'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("    timestamp: EpochMillis","    timestamp: EpochSeconds")
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='billing/api.py'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('"timestamp": record["timestamp"]}','"timestamp": to_millis(record["timestamp"])}')
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
grep -n "import" billing/api.py | head -20; grep -n "EpochMillis" billing/models.py

sed -i 's/^from \.engine import BillingEngine/from .clock import to_millis\n&/' billing/api.py && sed -n 180,195p billing/models.py && echo '{"summary": "Usage records now store timestamp in epoch seconds, converting from milliseconds at the usage/API boundary and back in the API response."}' > answer.json && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -3; .venv/bin/python -m ruff check billing

sed -i '' 's/^from \.engine import BillingEngine/from .clock import to_millis\
&/' billing/api.py && sed -i '' 's/import to_millis, to_seconds/import to_seconds/' billing/usage.py && echo '{"summary": "Usage records now store timestamp in epoch seconds, converting from milliseconds at the usage/API boundary and back in the API response."}' > answer.json && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -3; .venv/bin/python -m ruff check billing
